prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-04-29. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.28 |
| Retained earnings       | 302,526M |
| Current liabilities     | 136,661M |
| Current assets          | 175,329M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 414,367M |
| Total liabilities       | 279,861M |
| Total assets            | 694,228M |
| EBIT / operating income | 38,398M |
| Revenue                 | 82,886M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-04-29, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided balance sheet shows modest leverage (total liabilities of ~40% of assets, or D/E of 0.68) and solid liquidity (current ratio of 1.28). Profitability is exceptionally strong (EBIT margin of ~46%), with a large retained-earnings buffer, all of which map to very low expected default risk on a through-the-cycle basis.
DECISION: AA
(The data are also consistent with AA+ or AA-, but the single current-ratio observation prevents finer distinction.)
